links.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT-4 treatment recommendations with AAOS clinical practice guidelines
links.effect: 90% (90 of 100) concordant with AAOS CPGs; 78% (78 of 100) concordant with attending plan; 100% for fracture and hip/knee arthritis, 3 of 10 discordant for carpal tunnel syndrome.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4 provided treatment recommendations in accordance with the AAOS CPGs in 90% (90 of 100) of clinical vignettes.

links.outcome: Errors in AI treatment recommendations that would require clinician verification
links.effect: 10 of 100 recommendations diverged from CPGs, mainly misjudged severity and progression, failure to integrate patient factors, and missed contraindication to surgery.
links.quote: In these situations, ChatGPT-4 most often struggled to correctly interpret injury severity and progression, incorporate patient factors (such as lifestyle or comorbidities) into decision-making, and recognize a contraindication to surgery.

screen.reason: Evaluates ChatGPT-4 treatment recommendations against clinical practice guidelines using offline multimodal clinical vignettes (text and representative radiographs) without testing a specific implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
